To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the clinical course of COVID‐19 in immunosupressed patients is similar to immunocompe­tent patients.
transplanted patients with COVID‐19 seem to have a similar course as immunocompetent individuals, but with an attenuated inflammatory response.
the immunosuppressed solid organ recipients with SARS‐Cov‐2 infection have an attenuated early inflammatory response, which might be beneficial for the clinical course of the disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical course of transplanted patients with COVID‐19, which might be of importance for the management of these patients.
the clinical course of transplanted patients with COVID‐19 in comparison with non‐transplated patients and the impact of immunosuppression.
the question, how immunosuppression affects COVID‐19 in solid organ transplant patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
immunosuppression does not increase the risk for COVID‐19 in solid organ recipients.
immunosuppression in transplanted recipients does not worsen COVID‐19, but attenuates the early inflammatory response.
COVID‐19 in solid organ transplant patients is a severe but manageable condition, which can be treated with the same measures as in non‐immunosuppressed patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
immunosuppressed organ recipients with COVID ‐ 19 are at risk to develop severe pneumonia and require intensive care.
immunosuppression in transplanted COVID‐19 patients is safe and might even be beneficial.
immunosuppressed transplant patients with COVID‐19 are more prone to develop a severe disease but have an attenuated inflammatory response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immunosuppression of organ transplant recipients does not seem to be a risk factor per se for severe COVID‐19.
immunosuppression does not seem to worsen the clinical outcome in patients with COVID‐19.
immunosuppression should be maintained in transplanted individuals.
